{"parentUuid":"01b69321-c6bc-42b8-9fbe-36a61fedfebc","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"d6548c2f-0d26-4ebb-a063-55d083001b47","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019hKjhZBJzTTbiieYQtUme9","type":"tool_result","content":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n# Triage Labels\n\nThe skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. This file maps those roles to the actual label strings used in this repo's issue tracker.\n\n| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |\n| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\n| `needs-triage`             | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |\n| `needs-info`               | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |\n| `ready-for-agent`          | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |\n| `ready-for-human`          | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |\n| `wontfix`                  | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |\n\nWhen a skill mentions a role (e.g. \"apply the AFK-ready triage label\"), use the corresponding label string from this table.\n\nEdit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use.\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"My CMS\")\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n\"\"\"T00: the walking skeleton. These pass in the fresh template.\n\nDo not delete them. If a change breaks them, the change broke the app's front\ndoor.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef test_admin_console_answers(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/admin\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    assert \"hello admin\" in response.text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_public_home_answers(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n\n\ndef test_publish_writes_a_site(tmp_path):\n    from app.publish import render_site\n\n    out = render_site(tmp_path / \"site\")\n    assert (out / \"index.html\").exists() and (out / \"style.css\").exists()\n\n\ndef test_published_html_uses_relative_paths(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Root-absolute paths break on GitHub Pages project URLs (rubric F2).\"\"\"\n    from app.publish import render_site\n\n    html = (render_site(tmp_path / \"site\") / \"index.html\").read_text()\n    assert 'href=\"/' not in html and 'src=\"/' not in html\n<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<head>\n  <meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n  <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n  <title>{% block title %}{{ title }}{% endblock %}</title>\n  <link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"{{ css_path | default('style.css') }}\">\n</head>\n<body>\n  <header><a href=\"{{ home_path | default('index.html') }}\">{{ title }}</a></header>\n  <main>{% block content %}{% endblock %}</main>\n  <footer><small>IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2</small></footer>\n</body>\n</html>\n[]","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"a1ff6b5b-4909-4878-a9bc-82eb985cb7c2","timestamp":"2026-10-24T14:31:15.670Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n# Triage Labels\n\nThe skills speak in terms of five canonical triage roles. This file maps those roles to the actual label strings used in this repo's issue tracker.\n\n| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning                                  |\n| -------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |\n| `needs-triage`             | `needs-triage`       | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue  |\n| `needs-info`               | `needs-info`         | Waiting on reporter for more information |\n| `ready-for-agent`          | `ready-for-agent`    | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent  |\n| `ready-for-human`          | `ready-for-human`    | Requires human implementation            |\n| `wontfix`                  | `wontfix`            | Will not be actioned                     |\n\nWhen a skill mentions a role (e.g. \"apply the AFK-ready triage label\"), use the corresponding label string from this table.\n\nEdit the right-hand column to match whatever vocabulary you actually use.\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n {"parentUuid":"9e5c96c5-b422-4435-982e-fd7ef9547fb2","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgMDwmHqrsEPaZgqUTecz","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Before I write the spec I have to check two things with you, because the code contradicts our glossary.\n\n**1. `CONTEXT.md` gets Deploy wrong.** `app/cli.py` and the manual (§ \"Deploy\") split it into two commands. `cms publish` only renders `site/` from the published rows. `cms deploy` pushes `site/` to `gh-pages`. Our **Deploy** entry says \"`cms publish` performs a Deploy (rebuild **and** push),\" which is wrong, and I suggested that wording in round 1. The term \"Deploy\" is still right. Only the sentence about the commands is wrong.\n\n➡️ Change the entry to: \"Deploy is two commands: `cms publish` renders the Public site into `site/`, and `cms deploy` pushes it live.\" I'd make this a one-line fix to `CONTEXT.md` in the spec commit.\n\n**2. Where an Admin starts a Deploy and a Backup.** Today both run from the terminal, and the CLI has no login. So \"only Admins Deploy and Backup\" holds only because the terminal is the President's.\n- (a) **Terminal only.** The console just shows a \"changes not yet live\" notice. Simplest option, and the role rule is enforced by who holds the laptop.\n- (b) **Admin-only console buttons** that call the same render, push, and backup code. The role rule is enforced and testable, but pushing to git from a web request adds failure modes, such as missing credentials.\n\n➡️ **(a)**. Editors work while the President is in the room. The console's permission rules already give plenty of evidence for capability 2 without these buttons.\n\n**3. Test seams.** I'd use the two seams the template already provides, and add nothing new:\n- **The HTTP app** through `TestClient`, plus the `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixture in `tests/conftest.py`. This covers login and logout, every role rule, CRUD for Recaps, Trips and Pages, Submit, Send back, Publish, the dashboard counts, the list filters, Preview, user management, and Deactivate.\n- **`render_site(out)`** into a `tmp_path`, which covers capability 7. The tests check that Drafts and Submitted Recaps never appear, that sanitizing strips `<script>` tags and external links and images, that the Navigation bar is built from Published Pages, that Trips with no Published Recap are hidden, and that all paths are relative. This follows the existing `tests/test_t00.py`.\n- **`cms backup`** is called through the existing `main(argv)` CLI entry point and checked for a dated archive. This is a light use of a seam that already exists.\n\nDo these seams match what you expect? And do you agree with 1 (the fix) and 2(a)? Once you answer, I'll write the spec and publish it as a GitHub issue labelled `ready-for-agent`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3034,"cache_read_input_tokens":115786,"output_tokens":1153,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":213},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3034,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1153,"cache_read_input_tokens":115786,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3034,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3034},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"a3bf1cf9-480e-47c5-b4d4-104b0ea7563b","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CgMDwkvXTcdzb3L4iRuFN","requestRef":"8fdf66d9-8fbc-4705-bad4-64b8068b9f05","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","attributionSkill":"to-spec","type":"assistant","uuid":"c1ba94d0-e0d7-427b-ae59-c43ac844eba9","timestamp":"2026-10-24T14:31:43.295Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"3c83bfcc-3eab-41bd-893a-8b0e0abb030e","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

A Deploy is two commands: `cms publish` renders the Public site into `site/` (the assignment's name, despite meaning Deploy's first half), and `cms deploy` pushes it live.","originalFile":"# Kenyon Model UN Recaps\n\nA content system where the Kenyon Model UN club's officers publish recaps of the club's conference trips for the Kenyon community.\n\n## Content\n\n**Trip**:\nOne conference journey the club made, such as the Chicago conference. A Trip carries its own required Summary of what the trip was, and groups the Recaps written about it. A Trip appears on the Public site only once it has at least one Published Recap, and it can be deleted only while it has no Recaps.\n_Avoid_: Event, conference (as the record's name)\n\n**Summary**:\nAn Admin-written overview on a Trip: the conference, where it was, and what happened overall. Readers see it at the top of the Trip's page.\n_Avoid_: Description, intro\n\n**Recap**:\nOne club member's personal account of exactly one Trip. A Recap has a title, a Slug, a Markdown body with optional Images, a Byline, an Owner, and records of when it was created, last edited, and Published. It is written by an Editor, or entered by an Admin for a Contributor. Recaps are individual anecdotes, while the Trip's Summary says what the trip was. A Trip can have several Recaps.\n_Avoid_: Post, blog, article\n\n**Slug**:\nThe short, URL-safe name that identifies a Trip, Recap, or Page in the public site's addresses, such as `2026-chicago` or `chicago-food-crawl`. A Trip's Slug is unique among Trips, a Recap's within its Trip, and a Page's among Pages. A Page cannot take a Slug the site already uses, such as `trips` or `images`.\n_Avoid_: Permalink, path, handle\n\n**Byline**:\nThe writer's name and class year shown on a Recap, such as \"by Jane Doe '27\". Both parts are required. An Editor's or Admin's Byline comes from their Account, and an Admin types a Contributor's Byline by hand. The Byline is separate from the Recap's Owner.\n_Avoid_: Author (an Admin who typed a Recap in is not its writer)\n\n**Owner**:\nThe Account a Recap or Page belongs to: the Editor who wrote it, or the Admin who created it or entered it for a Contributor. \"Their own Recap\" means a Recap they Own.\n_Avoid_: Author, creator\n\n**Image**:\nA photo uploaded to a Recap and placed inline in its body, always with alt text. Images belong to Recaps only. Recaps show only uploaded Images, never ones hosted elsewhere.\n_Avoid_: Media, attachment, embed\n\n**Page**:\nStanding content about the club that is not tied to a Trip, such as \"About the club\" or \"Officers and contact\". A Page has a title, a Slug, a text-only Markdown body, a Draft or Published status, an Owner, and records of when it was created and last edited. Only Admins create, edit, or delete Pages.\n_Avoid_: Static page, post\n\n**Body**:\nThe Markdown text of a Recap or Page. A Body never links to outside sites or shows images hosted elsewhere.\n_Avoid_: Content, text (for this field)\n\n**Navigation bar**:\nThe list of links across the top of the public site: a Home link first, then the Published Pages in the order Admins set.\n_Avoid_: Menu, header links\n\n## Publishing\n\n**Public site**:\nThe static website the Kenyon community reads: Trips that have a Published Recap, their Published Recaps, the Published Pages, and the Navigation bar. Deploy produces it. Nothing else reaches it.\n_Avoid_: Blog, front end, live site\n\n**Draft**:\nA Recap's or Page's status while it is still being written. Every Recap and Page starts as a Draft, and Drafts never leave the database.\n\n**Submitted**:\nA Recap's status once its Editor says it is finished and ready for an Admin to review. Nobody but an Admin can change it from here.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review\n\n**Published**:\nA Recap's or Page's status once an Admin has approved it for the public site. It is not visible to readers until the next Deploy.\n\n**Submit**:\nAn Editor moving their own Recap from Draft to Submitted.\n\n**Send back**:\nAn Admin returning a Submitted Recap to Draft so its Editor can revise it.\n_Avoid_: Reject\n\n**Publish / Unpublish**:\nMoving a Recap or Page to Published, or from Published back to Draft. Only Admins Publish or Unpublish.\n_Avoid_: using \"publish\" for rebuilding the site\n\n**Deploy**:\nRebuilding the Public site from the Trips, Published Recaps, and Published Pages, and pushing it live. Only Admins deploy. The assignment names the command `cms publish`. That command performs a Deploy, despite its name.\n_Avoid_: Publish (for this action), build, push\n\n**Backup**:\nA dated archive of the database and uploaded Images, kept somewhere private outside the repository. It is the only copy of Drafts and Recap sources if the Console laptop is lost. Only Admins make Backups.\n\n## Operations\n\n**Console laptop**:\nThe single machine (the President's) that runs the admin console and holds the one real database. Admins work on it, and Editors log in on it during the Sunday club meetings.\n\n**Handover**:\nThe yearly transfer to new officers: outgoing Admins create the incoming Admins' Accounts, incoming Admins Deactivate the outgoing ones, and the Console laptop or latest Backup moves with them.\n\n## People\n\n**Account**:\nOne person's login to the admin console, carrying their name, class year, and role (Admin or Editor). An Account is either active or Deactivated.\n_Avoid_: User (in prose), profile, login\n\n**Deactivate**:\nAn Admin switching off an Account so it can no longer log in. Its Recaps, Pages, and Bylines stay as they are. The last active Admin can never be Deactivated.\n_Avoid_: Delete, remove, ban\n\n**Admin**:\nThe club's President or Vice President. Admins can do everything an Editor can, and also Publish and Unpublish, Send back, create, edit, and delete Trips, create, edit, and delete Pages, create Accounts, change an Account's role, Deactivate Accounts, Deploy, and make Backups. They can edit or delete any Recap and enter one on a Contributor's behalf.\n_Avoid_: Officer (in the system), superuser\n\n**Editor**:\nA club member with their own Account who writes their own Recaps as Drafts, adds Images with alt text to them, and Submits them. An Editor can edit or delete their own Recap only while it is a Draft. The President and VP decide which members become Editors, and an Admin creates the Account. An Editor cannot Publish or Unpublish, create Trips, create or edit Pages, manage Accounts, Deploy, make Backups, or edit another person's Recap.\n_Avoid_: Author, writer, contributor (for this role)\n\n**Contributor**:\nA member whose writing an Admin enters for them, for example because they missed a Sunday meeting and emailed it in. A Contributor has no Account of their own.\n_Avoid_: Editor (for this role), author, writer\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":72,"oldLines":7,"newStart":72,"newLines":7,"lines":[" _Avoid_: using \"publish\" for rebuilding the site"," "," **Deploy**:","-Rebuilding the Public site from the Trips, Published Recaps, and Published Pages, and pushing it live. Only Admins deploy. The assignment names the command `cms publish`. That command performs a Deploy, despite its name.","+Rebuilding the Public site from the Trips, Published Recaps, and Published Pages, and pushing it live. Only Admins deploy. A Deploy is two commands: `cms publish` renders the Public site into `site/` (the assignment's name, despite meaning Deploy's first half), and `cms deploy` pushes it live."," _Avoid_: Publish (for this action), build, push"," "," **Backup**:"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"fd3eed81-960a-4ba6-bfbe-c31583889c3d","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"3c83bfcc-3eab-41bd-893a-8b0e0abb030e","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"2504066b-fbd1-4d31-bceb-9dde7c692cd3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgMEE1HR3SaV5MVzrkDG4","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_017SkHTzCD4689Z7dGaHds3c","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrewv-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/3c83bfcc-3eab-41bd-893a-8b0e0abb030e/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"Vocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`. Decisions behind it: ADR-001 (local admin console, static Public site), ADR-002 (stack), ADR-003 (Editors write at the Sunday meetings; only Admins Publish).\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon Model UN club has no website. Trip recaps go on Instagram, where they sink in the feed, so nobody in the Kenyon community can look back at a past Trip. The President and Vice President want a place where members' Recaps of each Trip (where the team went, how the competition went, what they explored and ate) are published with photos and stay findable. Members need to be able to write their own Recaps. The officers must stay in control of what reaches readers, and no member can ever change another member's work or touch accounts.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with two halves:\n\n- An **admin console** that runs only on the **Console laptop**. Admins and Editors log in to it. Editors write their own Recaps at the Sunday club meetings and Submit them. Admins review, edit, Send back, or Publish them. Admins also manage Trips, Pages, and Accounts, and enter Recaps for Contributors who email their writing in.\n- A static **Public site** that an Admin Deploys from the terminal. It lists Trips newest first. Each Trip page shows its Summary and then its Published Recaps. Admin-written Pages, such as \"About the club\", form the Navigation bar. A footer link sends readers to Instagram for discussion. Only Published content reaches the Public site, and all of it is sanitized.\n\nAn Admin can also take a dated Backup of the database and Images with `cms backup`, so losing the laptop doesn't lose the club's writing.\n\n## User Stories\n\n**Login and Accounts**\n\n1. As an Admin, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can use Admin powers on the Console laptop.\n2. As an Editor, I want to log in with my own Account at the Sunday meeting, so that my Recaps are mine and nobody else's.\n3. As any logged-in person, I want to sign out, so that the next member at the laptop can't act as me.\n4. As an anonymous visitor to the console, I want to be redirected to the login page from every console page, so that nothing in the console is reachable without an Account.\n5. As an Admin, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n6. As a person who typed a wrong password, I want a generic \"email or password is incorrect\" message, so that the login page doesn't reveal which emails have Accounts.\n7. As an Admin, I want a Deactivated Account to be unable to log in, and any session it already has to stop working, so that a member who leaves the club loses access immediately.\n\n**Roles and permissions**\n\n8. As an Admin, I want Editors to get a 403 or a redirect on every Admin-only page and action, so that the Editor role is genuinely limited.\n9. As an Editor, I want to create Recaps, edit and delete my own Drafts, add Images to them, and Submit them, so that I can contribute without waiting on an officer.\n10. As an Admin, I want an Editor to be unable to Publish or Unpublish anything, so that Published always means an Admin approved it.\n11. As an Editor, I want to be refused when I try to view, edit, Submit, or delete another person's Recap, so that nobody can tamper with my writing.\n12. As an Editor, I want my Recap locked against my own edits once it is Submitted or Published, so that what an Admin reviewed doesn't change underneath them.\n13. As an Admin, I want to do everything an Editor can, and also edit or delete any Recap, so that I can fix typos and take down anything inappropriate.\n\n**Trips**\n\n14. As an Admin, I want to create a Trip with a conference name, host city, start date, end date, and Summary, so that Recaps have something to belong to.\n15. As an Admin, I want the Trip's Slug suggested from its year and city (such as `2026-chicago`) and editable, so that addresses are readable.\n16. As an Admin, I want to edit any Trip, so that I can correct its Summary or dates later.\n17. As an Admin, I want deleting a Trip refused while it still has Recaps, so that Recaps are never lost along with their Trip.\n18. As an Editor, I want to pick the Trip my Recap is about from a list, so that I can't misspell or invent a Trip.\n\n**Recaps**\n\n19. As an Editor, I want to write a Recap with a title, a Slug, and a Markdown Body, so that I can tell my story with basic formatting.\n20. As an Editor, I want the Slug suggested from the title, so that I don't have to think about URLs.\n21. As an Admin, I want a Recap's Slug to be unique within its Trip, with a clear error on a clash, so that two Recaps never share an address.\n22. As an Editor, I want my Byline (name and class year) filled in from my Account, so that I'm credited correctly without typing it.\n23. As an Admin entering a Contributor's emailed Recap, I want to type their name and class year as the Byline, so that the Contributor is credited and not me.\n24. As an Admin, I want every Recap to record its Owner and when it was created, last edited, and Published, so that I know who is responsible for it and how fresh it is.\n25. As an Admin, I want saving or Submitting a Recap with no Body text to be refused, so that no Recap is just photos.\n26. As an Editor, I want to Submit my finished Draft, so that the Admins know it's ready to review.\n27. As an Admin, I want to Send back a Submitted Recap to Draft, so that its Editor can revise it.\n28. As an Admin, I want to Publish a Draft or Submitted Recap, so that it goes out with the next Deploy.\n29. As an Admin, I want to Unpublish a Published Recap back to Draft, so that I can take it down at the next Deploy.\n30. As an Admin editing or Unpublishing a Published Recap or Page, I want a notice that the change is \"still live until you Deploy\", so that I don't assume readers already see the change.\n31. As an Editor, I want to delete my own Recap while it is a Draft, so that I can abandon a false start.\n\n**Images**\n\n32. As an Editor, I want to upload a JPEG, PNG, or WebP photo of up to about 5 MB to my Recap, with required alt text, so that my Recap has pictures that screen readers can describe.\n33. As an Editor, I want the console to give me a ready-to-paste Markdown snippet with my alt text filled in after an upload, so that I can place the photo where I want it in my Body.\n34. As an Admin, I want uploads of any other file type, or larger files, refused with a clear message, so that the Public site doesn't fill up with huge or unsafe files.\n35. As an Admin, I want Publish refused while the Body has an image without alt text, so that the Public site stays accessible.\n36. As an Admin, I want a Recap's Images deleted along with the Recap, so that orphaned photos don't pile up.\n\n**Pages and Navigation bar**\n\n37. As an Admin, I want to create, edit, and delete Pages (title, Slug, text-only Markdown Body, Draft or Published), so that the club has an \"About\" page and an \"Officers and contact\" page.\n38. As an Admin, I want each Page to record its Owner and when it was created and last edited, so that Pages are accountable like Recaps.\n39. As an Admin, I want to set a number for each Page's position in the Navigation bar, so that I control the order of the links.\n40. As an Admin, I want a Page Slug refused if it is reserved (`trips`, `images`, `admin`, `login`) or already used by another Page, so that addresses never collide.\n41. As an Editor, I want the Pages area to be closed to me, so that the role boundary is obvious.\n\n**Admin console**\n\n42. As an Admin, I want a dashboard showing counts of Recaps by status (Draft, Submitted, Published), Trips, Pages by status, and active Accounts, so that I can see at a glance what needs attention.\n43. As an Editor, I want my dashboard to show counts of my own Recaps by status, so that I know what I still owe.\n44. As an Admin, I want a \"changes not yet live\" notice on the dashboard whenever content has changed since the last `cms publish`, so that I remember to Deploy.\n45. As an Admin, I want a content list of Recaps that I can filter by status, by Trip, and by Owner, with Submitted Recaps shown first, so that I can find what to review quickly.\n46. As an Editor, I want the content list to show only my own Recaps, filterable by status and Trip, so that I see my own work and nobody else's.\n47. As an Admin, I want a Pages list I can filter by status, so that I can find Drafts.\n48. As an Editor or Admin, I want a Preview button on the Recap and Page editor that reloads the page showing the sanitized, rendered Body exactly as readers will see it, so that I can check formatting and Image placement before saving or Submitting.\n49. As any console user, I want every form to carry a CSRF token, and any submission without a valid one refused, so that another website can't make my browser act for me.\n\n**Account management (Admin only)**\n\n50. As an Admin, I want to create an Account with an email, name, class year, role, and initial password, so that the members the President and VP chose can log in.\n51. As an Admin, I want to change an Account's role between Editor and Admin, so that officer changes can be handled.\n52. As an Admin, I want to Deactivate an Account while its Recaps, Pages, and Bylines stay, so that departing members lose access without their writing disappearing.\n53. As an Admin, I want Deactivating or demoting the last active Admin refused, so that the club can never lock itself out.\n54. As outgoing officers at Handover, we want to create the incoming Admins' Accounts and have them Deactivate ours, so that control transfers cleanly each year.\n\n**Public site and Deploy**\n\n55. As a Kenyon reader, I want the home page to list Trips newest first, so that I see the latest Trip immediately and can scroll back to older ones.\n56. As a reader, I want each Trip's page to show its Summary and then its Published Recaps in the order they were Published, with their Bylines, so that I get the overview and then each member's story.\n57. As a reader, I want a Trip to appear only once it has at least one Published Recap, so that I never land on an empty Trip.\n58. As a reader, I want a Navigation bar with Home first, then the Published Pages in the order the Admins set, so that \"About the club\" is always one click away.\n59. As a reader, I want a footer link to the club's Instagram for discussion, so that I can react to a Recap even though the site has no comments.\n60. As an Admin, I want `cms publish` to write only Published Recaps and Pages, and only Trips that have a Published Recap, into `site/`, so that Drafts and Submitted Recaps never leak.\n61. As an Admin, I want every Body sanitized when it is rendered, with scripts and raw HTML stripped and external links and external images removed, so that nothing harmful or off-site reaches readers.\n62. As an Admin, I want every link and image in `site/` to be a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n63. As an Admin, I want only the Images of Published Recaps copied into `site/`, so that photos from Drafts never become public.\n64. As an Admin, I want `cms deploy` to push `site/` live, so that a Deploy is `cms publish` followed by `cms deploy`.\n\n**Backup and seed data**\n\n65. As an Admin, I want `cms backup` to write one dated archive containing the database and all uploaded Images to a folder I choose outside the repository, so that I can keep a private copy on the club's Drive.\n66. As an Admin, I want `cms backup` to refuse to write inside the repository, so that a Backup can never be committed by accident.\n67. As a grader, I want the seed script to create one Admin and one Editor (passwords from the environment), a Trip, Recaps in each status, and a Draft and a Published Page, so that I can try every capability on a fresh clone.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Storage.** SQLite through the standard library, at the existing database path setting. The schema:\n\n- **Account**: email (unique, used to log in), name, class year, role (`admin` or `editor`), argon2 password hash, active flag, created timestamp.\n- **Trip**: conference name, host city, start date, end date, Summary, Slug (unique), created and edited timestamps.\n- **Recap**: Trip, Owner (an Account), title, Slug (unique per Trip), Body (Markdown), Byline name, Byline class year, status (`draft`, `submitted`, `published`), and created, edited, and Published timestamps.\n- **Page**: Owner, title, Slug (unique), Body (Markdown), status (`draft`, `published`), nav position, and created and edited timestamps.\n- **Image**: Recap, stored file name, original type, size, alt text.\n- **Site state**: a single record holding when `cms publish` last ran, which the \"changes not yet live\" notice uses.\n\n**Byline.** The Byline is copied onto the Recap when it is created: from the Owner's Account, or typed by an Admin for a Contributor. Admins can edit it. Renaming or Deactivating an Account later doesn't rewrite existing Bylines.\n\n**Recap status machine.** Every Recap starts as a Draft.\n\n| From | To | Who |\n|---|---|---|\n| Draft | Submitted | the Editor who Owns it |\n| Submitted | Draft (Send back) | Admin |\n| Draft or Submitted | Published | Admin |\n| Published | Draft (Unpublish) | Admin |\n\nEditors may edit or delete only their own Drafts. Admins may edit or delete any Recap. Pages go between Draft and Published, and only Admins move them.\n\n**Permission policy.** A single module answers \"can this Account do this action to this object\". Every route asks it, so there are no ad-hoc role checks scattered across routes. Being logged out redirects to login. Being logged in but not allowed returns 403. The policy rereads the Account on every request, so a Deactivation or role change takes effect at once.\n\n**Login and sessions.** Login takes an email and password at `/login`, matching the existing `client_as` test fixture. Sessions use a signed cookie through the existing `itsdangerous` dependency. Sign out clears the session. Login failures show one generic message.\n\n**CSRF.** Each session has a token, rendered as a hidden field in every form that changes state. Any state-changing request without a matching token gets a 403. No new dependency.\n\n**Markdown rendering.** One function turns a Body into HTML: `markdown-it-py`, then `nh3` with an allowlist of formatting tags. It removes:\n- any link whose target is not relative,\n- any image whose source is not one of the Recap's own uploaded Images,\n- all raw HTML.\n\nPreview and `cms publish` both use this same function, so what Preview shows is what readers get.\n\n**Images.** Accepted types are JPEG, PNG, and WebP, checked by file content and not by extension, up to about 5 MB. Images are stored in an uploads folder that is gitignored and outside `site/`. The snippet the console offers is a relative `images/<file>` reference. `cms publish` copies a Published Recap's Images next to its page, so that relative reference resolves.\n\n**Admin console screens.**\n- Login.\n- Dashboard, with counts and the \"changes not yet live\" notice.\n- Recaps list with filters for status, Trip, and Owner (Owner for Admins only), Submitted first for Admins.\n- Recap editor with Preview, Image upload, and action buttons for the transitions above.\n- Trips list and editor.\n- Pages list (filter by status) and editor with Preview and nav position.\n- Accounts list and editor.\n\nAll console routes sit under `/admin`, except `/login` and `/logout`. Screens are server-rendered with Jinja. There is no JavaScript framework and no live preview (ADR-002).\n\n**Admin-only routes.** These must refuse Editors:\n- Trip create, edit, and delete.\n- All Page routes.\n- All Account routes.\n- Publish, Unpublish, and Send back.\n- Editing, Submitting, or deleting a Recap the Editor doesn't Own.\n\n**Public site rendering.** `render_site` writes:\n- the home page (Trips with a Published Recap, newest start date first),\n- one page per such Trip,\n- one page per Published Recap,\n- one page per Published Page,\n- the stylesheet,\n- copied Images.\n\nAddresses take the forms `trips/<trip>/`, `trips/<trip>/<recap>/` and `<page>/`, each as an index file. Every link is computed relative to the page's depth. The Navigation bar is Home followed by the Published Pages by nav position. The footer holds the Instagram link, read from a setting in the environment. Nothing that isn't Published is ever read by the renderer.\n\n**Deploy and Backup run from the terminal only.** Deploy is `cms publish` followed by `cms deploy`, both of which already exist. The console has no Deploy or Backup button. \"Only Admins Deploy and Backup\" holds because the terminal belongs to the President.\n\n**`cms backup`.** A new subcommand on the existing CLI. It takes the SQLite online-backup copy of the database and the uploads folder, and zips them with the standard library into `cms-backup-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.zip` in an output folder given as an argument. It refuses any output folder inside the repository. Backup archives are also gitignored as a second safeguard.\n\n**Seed data.** Extend the existing seed script. Its Admin and Editor emails match the test fixture, and passwords come from `CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` and `CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD`. It creates demo content in every status.\n\n**`CONTEXT.md`.** The Deploy entry now says that a Deploy is `cms publish` (render) plus `cms deploy` (push). It is corrected in the same commit that references this spec.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test drives the system from outside and checks what a user or reader would see: HTTP status codes, redirects, page text, and files written to `site/`. Tests don't reach into tables or private functions. They use only the seams that already exist, and no new seams are added.\n\n**Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Tests use `TestClient` with the `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. The fixtures may be extended so each test gets a temporary database with the demo Accounts seeded. That changes how the fixtures are set up, not which seam the tests use. The required tests are:\n\n- **Anonymous visitors**: requesting every console route redirects to login.\n- **Editors on Admin-only routes**: a table-driven test hits every Admin-only route and action listed above as an Editor and expects a 403 or a redirect for each one.\n- **Editors cannot Publish**: an Editor's Publish and Unpublish requests are refused, and the Recap's status stays the same.\n- **Editors cannot touch another person's Recap**: edit, Submit, and delete requests on someone else's Recap are refused, and the Recap is unchanged.\n- **Editors are locked out after Submit**: an Editor can't edit their own Recap once it is Submitted or Published.\n- **Passwords**: the stored password is an argon2 hash and never the plain text. Logging in with the right password works, and with a wrong one fails with the generic message. Signing out ends the session.\n- **Deactivation**: a Deactivated Account can't log in, and its existing session stops working. Deactivating or demoting the last active Admin is refused.\n- **Role changes**: after an Admin changes an Account's role, its permissions follow the new role.\n- **CSRF**: every state-changing form contains a token, and a POST without a valid token gets a 403.\n- **Recap rules**: Submit, Send back, Publish, and Unpublish each move the status as specified. An empty Body is refused. A Slug that clashes within its Trip is refused. Deleting a Trip that has Recaps is refused.\n- **Image rules**: wrong file types, oversized files, and missing alt text are refused. Publish is refused while the Body has an image without alt text.\n- **Dashboard**: the counts match the seeded data, for both an Admin and an Editor.\n- **Content list**: the status, Trip, and Owner filters return the right Recaps. Editors see only their own Recaps.\n- **Preview**: given a Body containing `<script>`, an external link, and an external image, Preview shows sanitized HTML with all three removed.\n\n**Seam 2: `render_site(out)` into `tmp_path`.** These tests follow the prior art in `tests/test_t00.py`. Using a seeded database, they check:\n\n- Draft and Submitted Recaps, Draft Pages, and Trips with no Published Recap are absent from the output.\n- Published content is present.\n- Body sanitization holds in the output.\n- The Navigation bar lists Home, then the Published Pages in nav order.\n- No `href=\"/` or `src=\"/` appears anywhere.\n- Only the Images of Published Recaps are copied.\n\n**Existing CLI entry point: `main(argv)`.** `cms backup` writes a dated archive containing the database and the uploads, and refuses an output folder inside the repository.\n\nThe tests in `tests/test_t00.py` must keep passing.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments on the Public site. This is a known gap, and the Instagram footer link stands in for it.\n- Images on Pages, as a possible later addition. Pages are text-only.\n- A hosted or remote admin console. Editors use the Console laptop (ADR-001, ADR-003).\n- Deploy and Backup buttons in the console.\n- Reactivating a Deactivated Account. Admins create a new Account instead (see Further Notes).\n- A live preview, a WYSIWYG editor, drag-and-drop, multi-site, tags and categories, and search.\n- Password reset by email. An Admin sets a new password instead.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n**Coverage of the seven required capabilities**\n\n| # | Capability | Where this spec covers it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Login: sign in and out, hashed passwords | Stories 1–7. Login, sessions and argon2 decisions. Password and Deactivation tests. |\n| 2 | Two roles with genuinely different permissions | Stories 8–13 and 41. Permission policy. Admin-only route list. Required 403-or-redirect and Recap-ownership tests. |\n| 3 | Posts (here, Recaps and Trips): CRUD, title, Slug, Markdown Body, draft and published, author, timestamps | Stories 14–31. Schema (Owner as author, Byline as the displayed author). Status machine. |\n| 4 | Pages, with published Pages in the nav | Stories 37–41 and 58. Page schema. Navigation bar rendering. |\n| 5 | Admin console: dashboard counts, filterable content list, editor with Preview | Stories 42–49. Console screens. Dashboard, content list and Preview tests. |\n| 6 | User management: Admin-only, create, change role, Deactivate, Deactivated users can't log in | Stories 50–54. Account schema and policy. Deactivation and role tests. |\n| 7 | Public site and publish: only published content, sanitized Markdown, nav from Pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths | Stories 55–64. Rendering and sanitizer decisions. Seam 2 tests. |\n\n**Reactivation.** Reactivating a Deactivated Account never came up while the design was settled. This spec leaves it out to keep the Account rules small. Raise it before ticketing if the officers want it.\n\n**Who can Deploy.** \"Only Admins Deploy and Backup\" is enforced by the Console laptop's terminal being the President's, not by code. This is a deliberate trade-off, made in the spec session.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3368,"cache_read_input_tokens":120170,"output_tokens":8440,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":80},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3368,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":8440,"cache_read_input_tokens":120170,"cache_creation_input_tokens":3368,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":3368},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_017SkHTzCD4689Z7dGaHds3c":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrewv-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/3c83bfcc-3eab-41bd-893a-8b0e0abb030e/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"Vocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`.
